data.one_liner: Provides easy access to system information like architecture, kernel, memory, OS, CPU, and user.
data.what_it_does: It retrieves hardware and operating system characteristics such as kernel architecture, bitness, version, operating system name, user details, and memory limits. It allows querying specific host system properties directly in Dart.
use_when: You need to detect the host operating system or architecture at runtime.
You want to query available physical or virtual memory.
You need user directory or identification details on desktop or mobile environments.
avoid_when: You need real-time polling of memory in a latency-sensitive UI loop on Windows (as synchronous PowerShell calls can be slow).
PowerShell is disabled or restricted by policy on the target Windows environment.
strengths: Simplifies retrieval of low-level system and hardware details.
Supports multiple platforms including Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, and Linux.
weaknesses: Windows memory queries spawn local PowerShell processes which can be slow and are not suited for tight polling loops.
May throw a StateError if Windows PowerShell/CIM fails or is blocked.
data.setup_notes: On Windows, PowerShell (powershell.exe) must be available on the PATH with CimCmdlets and local WMI/CIM providers enabled for memory queries.
